title: Notification fabric patterns — grooming notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a set of small, pragmatic UX patterns and backlog fragments we discussed in the 2025-01-22 grooming session about the notification "fabric" — how alerts, SLO triggers, and operator policies should be composed in the Console. Goal is to land a minimal, consistent mental model that supports: channel mapping by team/route, threshold policy composition, dedup/suppression semantics, and clear escalation flows for Dedicated/Private customers.

State: rough ideas + wireframe text sketches. Not final. Priority: medium (ties into PROD-482).

Key principles we agreed on (short):
- Treat notifications as first-class, composable objects: channels, policies, and templates are separate but linked.
- Keep default policies simple (onboarding = low noise) while exposing power via policy composition (AND/OR chains, multi-interval).
- Surface dedup and suppression explicitly in the UI; do not hide them behind toggles.
- SLO-to-alert mapping should be visible on the SLO page and editable inline (quick link to create a policy from an SLO).

High-level UX patterns (sketches in text):
1) Channel Palette (left column in alert rule editor)
- List of channels with small icons (Slack, PagerDuty, Email, Webhook, SMS, Console in-app).
- Channels can have tags (team, severity handled) and ownership metadata.
- Quick test button on hover and a small recent-delivery status (last 7 days).
- Wireframe note: channel insertion via drag or + button.

2) Policy Builder (center panel)
- Rows: source (metric/SLO/log), condition (threshold or anomaly), aggregation window, evaluation cadence.
- Allow boolean groups (any/all) and foldable time windows (e.g., 5m over 3 occurrences OR 15m sustained).
- UX micro pattern: inline examples next to fields — show a real-alert sample that would fire with current inputs.

3) Routing & Escalation (right panel)
- Stacked routing rules: primary channels, fallback channels, regional overrides.
- Each rule shows a short multiplex preview: e.g., "Primary: pagerduty-prod -> If no ack in 10m -> fallback to oncall-email + slack-team".
- Option to set per-rule cooldowns and per-channel rate limits.

Policy composition examples (to be added to backlog as small tickets):
- Simple threshold: p90 latency > 750ms for 5m -> send to slack-service-team. (AC: button to create from SLO page)
- Composite (SLO + error-spike): SLO error budget burn > 2% in 1h OR error-rate increase > 3x baseline in 5m -> page oncall.
- Maintenance-aware policies: auto-suppress alerts if a linked deployment marker exists in the last 10m and suppression is allowed by team policy.

Deduplication & Suppression semantics (important):
- Dedup key model: by default dedupe by route + rule id + normalized signature (stack trace/text). Allow override to include request id or host.
- Suppression windows: global quiet hours per-team + ad-hoc mute for a rule (timeboxed).
- Visible timeline in the alert details UI showing: first match, last notified, suppressed intervals, ack history.

Example notification templates (templates stored centrally; rendered preview):
- Title: [ALERT] {service} {env} — {metric} {direction} {value}
- Body: context lines: SLO: {slo_name} | Rule: {rule_name} | Example trace: {trace_sample_link} | Suggested remediation: {runbook_link}
- Template variables should be discoverable via "insert variable" UI (autocomplete).

Backlog tickets (groomed to small pieces):
- NF-101: Channel quick-test UX + recent delivery indicator (2d).
- NF-102: Inline sample alert preview while editing policy (3d).
- NF-103: SLO -> New policy quickflow (1d). Related: link to PROD-482.
- NF-104: Dedup key override + preview of expected dedupe behavior (4d).
- NF-105: Maintenance-aware suppression toggle + project-level whitelist (2d).
- NF-106: Escalation timelines UI + ack countdown (3d).

Acceptance criteria (for NF-102 example):
- Editor shows a real-time example panel that updates when threshold or window fields change.
- Example uses synthetic sample data (not production) but mimics the distribution of the selected metric.
- Clicking "Preview as notification" opens the template renderer with variables filled.

Operational edge cases we must handle (notes for implementation):
- Multiple rules firing for same SLO: prefer the highest-severity rule unless user de-duplicates via policy. Document default behavior clearly.
- Cross-region customers: routing should match request region -> prefer local oncall then fallback global.
- Private deployments: channels may be internal-only (self-hosted webhook); show clear designation in channel list and prevent routing to public integrations by accident.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we allow user-defined dedup time windows per policy or only global? (Tradeoff: complexity vs control)
- How to represent policies that combine metrics from different sources (logs + metrics + SLOs) in a compact UI?
- Default escalation cadence: conservative (10m -> 30m -> page), or aggressive (5m -> 10m)? Need SRE input.
- How to surface cost implications of frequent firing (token counts for hosted evaluation vs Dedicated)? Slack with SRE and Billing to define.

Testing and rollout plan (quick):
- Feature-flag all new UX. Start with internal teams + 2 pilot customers.
- Telemetry: record actions (create, edit, test, preview), number of fired alerts, false-positive churn, mute usage.
- Soft-launch: beta label in console; gather feedback via linked survey in top-right of editor.

Implementation notes for engs (developer-facing):
- Keep server-side policy representation stable: a policy is {sources[], conditions[], routes[], suppression[]}. For now we only model it in the UI — server side will accept a similar flat schema.
- UI should not assume dedup uniqueness; it must display and allow modifying the dedup key without re-evaluating historical alerts.
- Provide a lightweight local simulator (same code path as real evaluation) for the inline preview.

Links / references from meeting:
- Slack thread: #console-alerts (search: "notification fabric demo 2025-01-22")
- Related RFC: Notification Fabric (confluence link above).

Next steps (short):
- Jordan: prototype inline preview components (due 2025-01-31).
- Sofia: mockups for routing stack + escalation timeline (due 2025-02-04).
- Maya: split backlog tickets, attach ACs, link to PROD-482 (done by 2025-01-28).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep onboarding defaults conservative. We get more pain from noisy alerts than from missed edge cases.
- Avoid "magic" auto-suppression without clear explanation — users distrust hidden behavior.

Draft ends here. Add screenshots/wireframes in a follow-up doc if we want to T-shirt variations for mobile vs desktop.
